title: Under His Wings
lead: A picture of God's protection, like a bird sheltering its young (Psalm 17:8; 91:4; Matthew 23:37). The Hebrew kanaf also means the corner of a garment, so the image links refuge with marriage (Ruth 3:9; Ezekiel 16:8) and with the tassels on Israel's clothes (Numbers 15:38).

sections.b: God carried Israel out of Egypt "on eagles' wings" (Exodus 19:4, KJV) and is pictured as an eagle hovering over its young (Deuteronomy 32:11). The psalms seek shelter "in the shadow of your wings" (Psalm 36:7; 57:1; 63:7), "in the shade of your wings" (Psalm 17:8) and "beneath his wings" (Psalm 91:4). Malachi promises "the sun of righteousness... with healing in its wings" (Malachi 4:2), using kanaf, and Jesus longs to gather Jerusalem "as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings" (Matthew 23:37). The same word names the corners of a garment, where Israel wore tassels (Numbers 15:38), and the edge of a cloak spread over a bride (Ezekiel 16:8).
